                    ### Question
                    A 4-month-old boy with a history of multiple infections presents with muscle stiffness. On physical exam, he is found to have carpopedal spasm as well as a heart murmur. Based on your clinical suspicion you decide to obtain a chest X-ray which shows a diminished shadow in the mediastinum. A mutation in which of the following chromosomes is the most likely cause of this patient's presentation?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Chromosome 5
opb. Chromosome 7
opc. Chromosome 17
opd. Chromosome 22
ope. Chromosome X

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation of muscle stiffness, carpopedal spasm, heart murmur, and a diminished shadow in the mediastinum on chest X-ray is highly suggestive of DiGeorge syndrome. DiGeorge syndrome is associated with a chromosome 22 mutation. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's presentation is a mutation in Chromosome 22.
